title: Journey - Walking Through Grief - Day 1: You are not alone

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, slow and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Walking Through Grief. <short pause> This is day one, You Are Not Alone. <short pause> I'm so sorry for your loss. <short pause> We'll walk slowly, and you can stop whenever you need to. <short pause> If grief ever makes you think of harming yourself, please call your local emergency number or a crisis line, or reach someone who can be with you.

After Jesus died, two of His friends set out on a road to a village called Emmaus. <short pause> They walked, and they talked, and they were sad. <short pause> And Jesus Himself came near, and walked along with them. <short pause> They didn't recognize Him. <short pause> But He was no less there. <short pause> Long before that road, Psalm thirty-four, verse eighteen had said where He could be found.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

parts.style: tender, soft, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: So you may not recognize Him today. <short pause> Grief can do that to our eyes. <short pause> It doesn't mean you've been left to walk this by yourself. <short pause> You don't have to catch up with God... <short pause> He has fallen into step with you.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: On that road, He asked them why they were sad. <short pause> And then He let them talk. <short pause> So tell Him, as you would tell someone walking beside you. <short pause> Their name. <short pause> What happened. <short pause> Or only, I don't have words yet. <short pause> He isn't in any hurry.

parts.style: prayerful, slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: Lord Jesus, I can't always see You on this road. <short pause> Match Your step to mine. <short pause> Stay when I'm quiet, and stay when I fall apart. <short pause> Walk with me. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, steady, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: When you next have to get up and cross a room, let those be your words. <short pause> Just three, at the speed of your feet... <short pause> walk with me. <short pause> Go gently.
